chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, who said:
I came to Khurāsān while I was a Wāqifī. I carried goods with me, and there was with me a patterned cloth in one of the bundles, but I was unaware of it and did not know its location.

So when I arrived in Marw and lodged in one of its dwellings, suddenly there was a Madinan man from among its muwallads, and he said to me: Abu al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام says to you: Send to me the patterned cloth that is with you. He said: So I said, Who informed Abu al-Ḥasan of my arrival, when I have only just arrived, and I do not have any patterned cloth with me?

So he returned to him and came back to me, and said: He says to you: Yes, it is in such-and-such a place, and its bundle is such-and-such. So I searched for it where he said, and I found it at the bottom of the bundle, and I sent it to him.

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّل: Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام, the Imam referred to in the report
key_terms.الرِّزَمِ: bundles or packed loads among the traveler’s goods
key_terms.خُرَاسَانَ: Khurāsān, the region to which the narrator traveled
key_terms.مَرْوَ: Marw, the city where the event took place
key_terms.مُوَلَّدِيهَا: those affiliated with or born among the people of that place
key_terms.وَاقِفٌ: a follower of the Wāqifī sect

ai.seo_question: How does this narration demonstrate the divinely granted knowledge of Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This report narrates an incident in which Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام informed a man of a hidden cloth among his belongings, despite the man himself being unaware of its location. The narration serves as a sign affirming the Imam’s divinely granted knowledge and supports the truth of the Imamate.
